quizName:
Hardest Questions in Maine
									  					
									  														  					Most difficult questions from your region.

questions.question: What should you do if you encounter an aggressive driver?
questions.explanation: When you meet an aggressive driver, the safest choice is to let them pass. Do not compete with other drivers. Always cooperate with other road users to prevent crashes.

questions.question: Is nighttime the safest time for cyclists to ride their bikes?
questions.explanation: Bicycles are hard to see in the dark, even with lights and reflectors. Both drivers and cyclists must be extra careful at night to avoid crashes.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your nervous system. It reduces alertness, concentration, and coordination. It also increases your reaction time.

questions.question: Why is night driving more difficult than day driving?

options.text: Cars overheat more quickly at night.
Visibility is reduced in the dark.
It is more likely to be raining at night.
You are more likely to encounter a motorcycle at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Visibility is reduced in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far ahead. Use your headlights and drive slowly enough to stop within the distance you can see.

questions.question: When is it important to slow down?

options.text: When the road is wet or slippery.

questions.explanation: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, at intersections, at railroad crossings, on hills, in sharp curves, near pedestrians, and on wet or slippery roads.

questions.question: What does alcohol cause?
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol hurts your vision, judgment, concentration, and coordination.

questions.question: What can cause distracted driving?

options.text: Talking or texting on a cellular phone.
Changing a radio station or CD.

questions.explanation: Drivers make many decisions every mile. You must focus fully on driving. Any other activity can be a dangerous distraction.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with sirens and flashing lights approaches, should you pull to the right and let it pass?
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with lights and/or sirens, pull to the right side of the road right away and let it pass.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells you it is not safe to enter this road or driveway from your direction. Turn around and find another route.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn in the direction shown by the arrow. In this case, you cannot turn right.

questions.question: What should you do if you are in a serious car crash?
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle and move it off the road if possible. If anyone is hurt, call 911. You must report the crash to police if someone is injured, someone dies, or there is more than $1,000 in property damage.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a stopped school bus with flashing lights and its signal arm extended?

options.text: Go 15 mph if no children are present.
Go at normal speed but watch for children.

questions.explanation: You must stop completely at a school bus with flashing lights and an extended signal arm. Wait until the arm is pulled back and the bus starts moving before you go. This rule applies whether you are driving in the same direction or the opposite direction.

questions.question: How can you identify an aggressive driver?

options.text: They make sudden, improper lane changes.
The number of passengers in their car.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make sudden, improper lane changes.
questions.explanation: Watch other drivers while you drive. An aggressive driver often makes sudden or improper lane changes. Do not challenge them. The safest choice is to move out of their way.

questions.question: What is important when driving on major highways?

options.text: Be ready to react to hazards.

questions.explanation: Stay alert on highways and be ready for unexpected hazards. Do not look at one thing for more than a few seconds to avoid highway hypnosis.

questions.question: What should you do if an aggressive driver is tailgating you?

options.text: Stare at the driver as they pass.

questions.explanation: Get out of the way of an aggressive driver. Avoid eye contact. Do not speed up or challenge them, as this will only make them angrier and more dangerous.

questions.question: What should you do before you start the car?

options.text: Make sure only backseat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only adults have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only children have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Before you start the car, buckle your seat belt and make sure all passengers buckle theirs.

questions.question: What should you do if you feel tired while driving?

options.text: Stop and rest or let someone else drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest or let someone else drive.
questions.explanation: Stop driving if you are tired. Take breaks every hour during long trips. Share driving with another person so you can each rest while the other drives.

questions.question: Should motorists keep a safe distance from cyclists?
questions.explanation: Drivers must keep a safe distance from cyclists when driving near them.

questions.question: What should you do if you miss your exit on an interstate?

options.text: Exit at the next exit and return to the exit you missed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit at the next exit and return to the exit you missed.
questions.explanation: Do not back up or turn around on the highway if you miss an exit. Go to the next exit and safely turn around.

questions.question: What should you do at a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights?

options.text: Drive around the gates if you do not see a train.
Stop behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, and proceed when the gates rise.
Slow down and drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, and proceed when the gates rise.
questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing when signs or flashing lights warn you of a train. It is illegal to drive around lowered gates.

questions.question: If you become too drowsy to drive safely, what should you do?

options.text: Open all windows and turn on the air conditioning.
Talk to a friend on the phone.

questions.explanation: When you are tired, you cannot drive safely. Your reactions slow down and your judgment gets worse. If you feel drowsy while driving, leave the road and rest.

questions.question: Anything that requires you to ____ could cause a crash.

options.text: Take your eyes off the road
Take your hands off the wheel
Take your attention away from driving

questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving, takes your eyes off the road, or takes your hands off the wheel.

questions.question: You must stop your vehicle in these situations:

options.text: At an intersection with a stop sign.
When a traffic officer orders you to stop.

questions.explanation: You must stop at stop signs, at red lights, and whenever a traffic officer tells you to stop.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing with no warning signals, you should slow down, look, and listen.
questions.explanation: If a railroad crossing has no warning lights or gates, slow down and look both ways. Listen for a train. Only cross when it is safe.

questions.question: Cell phones are a serious distraction while driving.
questions.explanation: Do not use cell phones while driving, except to report an emergency. Keep your full attention on the road.

questions.question: You missed your exit on the freeway. What should you do?

options.text: Make the turn quickly from your lane.
Continue to the next exit or turn where you can safely turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue to the next exit or turn where you can safely turn around.
questions.explanation: Do not back up on a freeway. Go to the next exit or turn where you can safely turn around.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, you should:

options.text: Make a U-turn through the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit.
Flag down a police officer to escort you back.

questions.explanation: Take the next exit. Do not stop, back up, or cross the median. These actions are illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: When stopped by police, you must show:
questions.explanation: You must carry your license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance. You must show all three when stopped by police.

questions.question: A truck or bus is making a right turn where you also need to turn right. What should you do?

options.text: Turn quickly before the truck or bus.
Wait for the truck or bus to complete its turn first.
Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the truck or bus to complete its turn first.
questions.explanation: Do not try to fit between a turning truck or bus and the curb. This can cause a serious crash. Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning before you turn.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This circular sign means a railroad crossing is ahead. Look and listen for trains before crossing.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?
questions.explanation: Alcohol and drugs harm many driving skills. They slow your reaction time, hurt your coordination, reduce your alertness, and make it hard to concentrate.

questions.question: When driving in work zones, you should:

options.text: Follow the driver in front of you closely.
Pass the driver in front of you as soon as you can.
Avoid tailgating and keep a safe following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid tailgating and keep a safe following distance.
questions.explanation: In work zones, keep a safe distance from barriers, trucks, equipment, workers, and other vehicles. Stay back from the car in front of you and do not tailgate.

questions.question: How can alcohol affect you?

options.text: It gives you a feeling of false confidence.

questions.explanation: Alcohol affects the brain parts that control judgment and self-control. It makes you feel overly confident and silly. It also slows your reaction time, hurts your balance, and weakens your vision and ability to judge distance.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.

questions.explanation: This sign is posted on one-way streets where you cannot enter. You may see it if you try to enter an expressway ramp going the wrong way.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers what they must do. When you see this sign, U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: If a traffic light is green and a police officer signals you to stop, you should:

options.text: Do what the vehicle in front of you does.

questions.explanation: You must follow a police officer's directions at all times, even if they go against traffic laws, signs, signals, or road markings.

questions.question: If you have an argument and you are angry, you should:

options.text: Loudly play the radio while driving so you won't think about your argument.
Take a few minutes to cool off before driving.
Drive on the interstate to let off steam.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to cool off before driving.
questions.explanation: Your emotions affect your driving ability. If you are very angry, excited, scared, worried, or sad, wait until you calm down before driving. You need to focus on driving without thinking about what upset you.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When you encounter an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Make sure they know you disapprove of their behavior.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: If another driver is driving dangerously around you, stay calm and create distance between your vehicles. Slow down and let them pass. Do not make eye contact or make rude gestures.

questions.question: Before turning, you should:
questions.explanation: Before turning, use your turn signal 3 to 4 seconds ahead of time so other drivers know what you plan to do.

questions.question: You want to turn right at a corner. A pedestrian with a guide dog is waiting to cross in front of you. What should you do?

options.text: Turn off your engine until the person crosses.
Tell the pedestrian when to cross.

questions.explanation: Always give the right-of-way to pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes.

questions.question: You are borrowing an unfamiliar vehicle from a friend. What should you do?

options.text: Don't worry about it because all vehicles are the same.
Don't tell your friend you are unfamiliar with the vehicle.
Ignore any obvious defects so you don't embarrass your friend.
Take a few minutes to learn where the controls are and how to use them before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to learn where the controls are and how to use them before driving.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, spend a few minutes learning the location and operation of the turn signals, headlights, windshield wipers, brakes, gear selector, and horn. Fix any defects before driving.

questions.question: You are driving and see animals near the road. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to scare them away.
Quickly move into the next lane.

questions.explanation: Slow down and proceed with caution when you see animals near the road. They may suddenly move into your path. Animals often travel in groups, so more may be nearby that you cannot see.

questions.question: A school bus has stopped with its stop arm extended. What should you do?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait.
Honk your horn and pass on the left side.
Keep driving once you think most children have exited.
Pass the bus before its door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when a school bus has its stop arm extended. Do not move until the stop arm is withdrawn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road has curves ahead.

questions.question: You had a bad experience at work and feel angry. When you reach your car, what should you do?

options.text: Play the radio loudly so you won't think about it.
Drive fast on the highway to let out your anger.
Take a few minutes to calm down before driving home.
Stop at a bar for drinks before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down before driving home.
questions.explanation: If you are angry or upset, take time to calm down before driving. Letting your emotions control your driving is dangerous to you and others on the road.

questions.question: You feel drowsy while driving. What should you do?
questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, stop at a rest area to take a nap, stretch, or let someone else drive. Caffeine pills and energy drinks are not a safe substitute for rest.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: These parking spaces are for people with disabled parking permits.
Traffic in this lane must turn in the direction of the arrow.
This lane is reserved for buses and vehicles with multiple passengers.

questions.correctAnswerText: These parking spaces are for people with disabled parking permits.
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces reserved for people with disabled parking permits.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Always signal, even if you don't see any traffic.
Signal only if there is traffic nearby.
Signal only when driving at night.
Signal only in heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal, even if you don't see any traffic.
questions.explanation: Always signal when turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb. Make it a habit and don't skip this important safety rule.

questions.question: Driving ability can be reduced by:
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires being in good physical condition. Alcohol, drugs, and lack of sleep can all affect your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: What should you do if you feel tired while driving?

options.text: Drive faster to reach your destination sooner.
Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.
questions.explanation: Watch for signs of fatigue while driving. You are too tired to drive safely if your eyes are closing, you drift between lanes, or you turn up the radio to stay awake. If you see these signs, park in a safe place and rest.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching railroad tracks?

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
Speed up to cross before the gate comes down.
Try to drive around a lowered gate.
Do not worry about how many tracks you need to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When you approach railroad tracks, look and listen for trains or other vehicles. Slow down and be prepared to stop.

questions.question: Orange signs are used in construction work zones to warn drivers.
questions.explanation: Most construction area signs are orange and diamond-shaped. Some signs are rectangular. These signs have reflective material so they are easy to see at night.

questions.question: What is the best thing to do if you get tired while driving?

options.text: Stop to rest or let another person drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to rest or let another person drive.
questions.explanation: If you get tired while driving, stop to rest or change drivers. Tiredness slows your thinking and reactions, which makes driving unsafe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Fines double in a work zone.

questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. They are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns drivers that bicycles may cross here.

questions.question: Like alcohol and other drugs, drowsiness can:
questions.explanation: Not sleeping enough causes poor driving. Like drugs and alcohol, sleepiness slows your reaction time, reduces awareness, and affects judgment.

questions.question: At a crosswalk, what must you do?

options.text: Construction workers must yield to you.

questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at street crossings if they follow traffic signals. If there is no traffic signal, you must stop for pedestrians in a marked or unmarked crosswalk.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Parking reserved for persons with disabilities.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parking reserved for persons with disabilities.
questions.explanation: This sign shows parking spaces reserved for vehicles with Persons with Disabilities license plates, Disabled Veteran license plates, or disabled parking placards.

questions.question: In a vehicle with airbags, where is the safest place for children age 12 and under to sit?

options.text: The bed of a pickup truck.

questions.explanation: Airbags help protect adults in crashes, but they can seriously hurt children. Children age 12 and under should sit in the back seat of vehicles with airbags.

questions.question: What should you do if you need to make an emergency stop on an interstate?

options.text: Use your horn to get passing cars to notice you.
Get out and flag down the next vehicle that passes.
Pull to the side, turn on emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side, turn on emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle if possible.
questions.explanation: If you must stop on an interstate shoulder, turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers. Stay inside your vehicle if you can. Traffic moves very fast on interstates, making it dangerous to stand or walk along the road.
